items.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018
items.q: because they’re not worldwide household name like Michael Jackson? No. And look what happened to him.

ctx.x: I’ll work on that. What is interesting, making it means many different things to many different people. I think you have to figure out what making it means to you and not what making it looks like to somebody else, or what somebody tells you making it means. For some people it’s just being debt free. You’re already, how much percentage of America is in debt first of all. So if you could just be debt free you are up in the higher percentage, upper echelon of like Americans and their finances. So maybe that’s…

their idea. Not everybody wants to be Beyoncé. Not everybody even should be, oh my God. You know? So there’s many different ideas of success and I think the sad part is that a lot of times people feel pressure to become as successful as other people say they should be. And success is so many different things. There are people that I never knew of until I got into the world of jazz. Never heard their name, I didn’t even know they existed. And then, but that doesn’t mean that they weren’t successful until I…
